summary: אָדָם is man: the kind God created male and female and named (Gen 1:27; 5:2), any human being, and the first man, whose name it is. אֲדָמָה is the ground: the soil that is tilled, the stuff the man and the beasts were formed from and return to, the face of the earth, and a people’s land. Scripture itself joins the two words, “Yahweh God formed the man (הָאָדָם), dust from the ground (הָאֲדָמָה)” (Gen 2:7; 3:19, 23). The third group is the colour red (אָדֹם, with its verb, אֲדַמְדָּם, אַדְמוֹנִי and the stone אֹדֶם), the colour of blood, wine and red stew, from which Esau was called Edom (Gen 25:30); Akkadian adamatu, “dark red earth”, and Arabic أُدْمَة, “tawny, the colour of the earth”, join the colour to the ground, though scripture nowhere says in so many words that the ground or the man is named from the colour.

words.gloss: man, mankind; a man, a human being; the man (Adam)
words.summary: A collective with no plural and no feminine: one human or all of them, men and women alike (Gen 5:2; Num 31:35). Where one person is meant scripture says “a son of אָדָם”, and for the many “the sons of אָדָם”. With the article in Gen 2–4 it is the first man; without it, from Gen 4:25, it is his name (see the name entry Adam). The key also counts the town Adam by the Jordan (Jos 3:16), which is a place and not a word of this entry.

senses.definition: The human kind as one whole, which God created male and female in his image and named אָדָם; the race that fills the earth, set beside the beasts as the other living creatures and distinct from them.

evidence.note: “Let us make אָדָם in our image … and let them rule”; “God created הָאָדָם in his image … male and female he created them”: singular in form, plural in what it names.
“Male and female he created them, and he blessed them and called their name אָדָם in the day they were created”: the word is the name of the kind, the woman included.
“When הָאָדָם began to multiply on the face of the ground and daughters were born to them.”
“I will wipe out הָאָדָם whom I created from the face of the ground, from אָדָם to beast to creeping thing to bird of the heavens”: man as one kind of creature among the others.
All flesh that moved on the earth expired, bird, cattle, beast, swarming thing, “and all הָאָדָם”.
“נֶפֶשׁ אָדָם, of the women who had not known a man, 32,000”: said of women.
“From the day that God created אָדָם on the earth.”
“אָדָם and beast you save, Yahweh.”
“I made the earth, הָאָדָם and the beast that are on the face of the earth.”
“I made earth, and אָדָם upon it I created.”
“God made הָאָדָם upright, but they have sought out many devices”: the singular taken up by “they”.
Paul: God “made of one every nation of men to dwell on all the face of the earth”.

senses.definition: With the article in Gen 2–4, the one man whom Yahweh God formed of dust from the ground, set in the garden and built the woman from: the first of the kind, from whom the rest come.

evidence.note: “Yahweh God formed הָאָדָם, dust from הָאֲדָמָה, and breathed into his nostrils breath of life, and הָאָדָם became a living soul”: the man is named beside the ground he was taken from.
Yahweh God took הָאָדָם and put him in the garden of Eden to work it and keep it.
The rib taken “from הָאָדָם” built into a woman and brought “to הָאָדָם”.
To the man: “until you return to הָאֲדָמָה, for out of it you were taken; for dust you are and to dust you shall return.”
Sent out of the garden “to work הָאֲדָמָה from which he was taken”; “he drove out הָאָדָם”.
“הָאָדָם knew Eve his wife.”
Paul quotes Gen 2:7 with both the word and the name: “the first man Adam (ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος Ἀδάμ) became a living soul”.
“The first man, out of earth, of dust (ἐκ γῆς χοϊκός)”: Paul’s reading of “dust from the ground”.

senses.gloss: a man, a human being; anyone
senses.definition: Any one human being, man or woman, with no regard to rank or sex: the word the law uses for “a person, anyone”, and with a negative “no one”.

evidence.note: “אָדָם, when any of you brings an offering to Yahweh”: anyone at all.
“אָדָם, when there is in the skin of his flesh a swelling”.
“This is the law: אָדָם, when he dies in a tent”.
“A man who strikes any נֶפֶשׁ אָדָם shall surely be put to death”: any human life.
“My statutes and my judgments, which הָאָדָם shall do and live by them”; quoted Rom 10:5; Gal 3:12.
“Not by bread alone does הָאָדָם live”; quoted by Jesus, Mat 4:4.
“For there is no אָדָם who does not sin”: no one.
“There is not a righteous אָדָם on earth who does good and does not sin.”
“הָאָדָם shall not see me and live”: no human being.
“He has told you, אָדָם, what is good”: an address to anyone who hears.
Ishmael, “a wild donkey of אָדָם”: joined to another noun to say what sort of human.

senses.gloss: man as against God: mortal, of flesh, not to be trusted in
senses.definition: Man in what he is beside God: flesh and not spirit, one who lies, changes and dies, whose breath is in his nostrils and whose days are a breath, so that trust in him is misplaced.

evidence.note: “Egypt is אָדָם and not אֵל, and their horses flesh and not spirit”: man is to God as flesh is to spirit.
To the prince of Tyre who said “I am a god”: “you are אָדָם and not אֵל”; again in Ezk 28:9, “in the hand of those who pierce you”.
“God is not a man (אִישׁ) that he should lie, nor a son of אָדָם that he should change his mind.”
“He is not אָדָם, to change his mind.”
“Not as הָאָדָם sees: for הָאָדָם looks at the eyes, but Yahweh looks at the heart.”
“Cease from הָאָדָם, whose breath is in his nostrils, for at what is he to be reckoned?”
“Do not trust in nobles, in a son of אָדָם in whom is no salvation: his breath goes out, he returns to his ground (לְאַדְמָתוֹ); in that day his thoughts perish”: אָדָם and אֲדָמָה together again.
“Yahweh, what is אָדָם that you know him? … אָדָם is like a breath; his days are as a passing shadow.”
“Surely like אָדָם you shall die.”
“אָדָם, born of woman, short of days and full of trouble.”
“Cursed is the man who trusts in אָדָם and makes flesh his arm, and whose heart turns from Yahweh.”
“Not to אָדָם is his way; it is not in a man who walks to direct his step.”
“It is better to take refuge in Yahweh than to trust in אָדָם.”

senses.gloss: (the likeness, the hand, the face of) a man
senses.definition: The human form, in the visions of Ezekiel and Daniel, where what is seen is described by its likeness to a man.

evidence.note: The four living creatures: “the likeness of אָדָם was theirs”; hands of אָדָם (1:8), the face of אָדָם (1:10).
On the likeness of the throne, “a likeness as the appearance of אָדָם upon it above”.
“One like the likeness of the sons of אָדָם touched my lips.”
The idol maker shapes wood “like the form of a man, like the beauty of אָדָם”.

evidence.locator: Gen.2.7, הָאָדָם → ἄνθρωπον, ἄνθρωπος; Psa.8.5, בֶן־אָדָם → υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου; Deu.8.3; Lev.18.5; Psa.118.6; Amo.9.12, אֱדוֹם → ἀνθρώπων; ἄνθρωπος renders אָדָם ×476

evidence.note: Gen 2:7 quoted: “the first ἄνθρωπος Adam became a living soul”.
Psa 8:5 quoted: “what is ἄνθρωπος that you remember him, or υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου that you visit him?”
Deu 8:3 quoted: “not by bread alone shall ἄνθρωπος live”.
Lev 18:5 quoted: “the ἄνθρωπος who does them shall live in them”; also Rom 10:5.
Psa 118:6 quoted: “I will not fear: what shall ἄνθρωπος do to me?”
James quotes Amo 9:12 as “that the rest of men (τῶν ἀνθρώπων) may seek the Lord”, where the Hebrew text reads “the remnant of Edom” (אֱדוֹם): the same consonants as אָדָם.
“ὁ, indecl. (Heb. אָדָם)”.

evidence.locator: Gen.5.2, אָדָם → αδαμ; Ἀδάμ renders אָדָם ×22

evidence.note: “The first man Adam became a living soul; the last Adam a life-giving spirit”: the Hebrew word carried into the Greek as a name, and used as a title of Christ.
“As in Adam all die, so also in the Christ all shall be made alive.”
“Death reigned from Adam to Moses … Adam, who is a type of the one to come.”
“Son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.”

parallels.note: “Man” and “son of man” set side by side, each word in either place; both of man as small and dying before God.

evidence.note: “What is אֱנוֹשׁ that you remember him, and a son of אָדָם that you visit him?”
The same pair turned about: אָדָם … בֶּן־אֱנוֹשׁ.
“Afraid of אֱנוֹשׁ who dies, and of a son of אָדָם who is given up as grass.”
“אֱנוֹשׁ, a maggot, and a son of אָדָם, a worm.”

parallels.note: Beside אִישׁ in parallel lines; where the two are told apart, “sons of אָדָם” are the common people and “sons of אִישׁ” men of standing.

evidence.note: “אָדָם is bowed down and אִישׁ is brought low.”
“Both sons of אָדָם and sons of אִישׁ, rich and poor together.”
“Sons of אָדָם are a breath, sons of אִישׁ a lie.”

parallels.note: Man and flesh as one thing.

evidence.note: “All flesh would expire together, and אָדָם return to dust.”
“Trusts in אָדָם and makes flesh his arm.”
“My spirit shall not strive in הָאָדָם for ever, in that he also is flesh.”

opposites.note: Man is what God is not.

evidence.note: “Favour and good understanding in the eyes of God and אָדָם”: the two before whom a person stands.

opposites.note: Man and beast, the two halves of the living creatures of the land; one fate in death.

evidence.note: Boils “on הָאָדָם and on the beast”.
Every firstborn in Egypt, “from אָדָם to beast”.
“As this one dies so that one dies, and one breath is for all, and הָאָדָם has no advantage over the beast.”
“אָדָם in honour does not abide; he is like the beasts that perish.”

phrases.gloss: a son of man: one human being

evidence.note: Yahweh’s address to Ezekiel, some ninety times in the book: “Son of אָדָם, stand on your feet.”
Gabriel to Daniel: “Understand, son of אָדָם.”
Quoted of Jesus in Heb 2:6.
“The man of your right hand, the son of אָדָם you made strong for yourself.”

phrases.gloss: the sons of man: human beings, people

evidence.note: “The heavens are Yahweh’s heavens, but the earth he has given to the sons of אָדָם.”
“When the Most High gave nations their inheritance, when he parted the sons of אָדָם.”
The city and tower “which the sons of הָאָדָם built”.
“You say, Return, sons of אָדָם.”

phrases.gloss: from man to beast: every living creature of the land
a human soul: a person, a human life, a human body

evidence.note: “He who touches the dead, any נֶפֶשׁ אָדָם, shall be unclean seven days”: a human corpse.
“Whoever sheds the blood of הָאָדָם, by הָאָדָם his blood shall be shed, for in the image of God he made הָאָדָם”: דָּם, אָדָם and (in דְּמוּת, Gen 5:1) “likeness” sound together in these chapters.

words.gloss: ground, soil; earth (as stuff); face of the earth; land
words.summary: Where אֶרֶץ is the earth under the heavens or a country by its borders, אֲדָמָה is the ground itself: what is tilled, what things are made of, what one stands on, and so a people’s own soil. The key also counts the town Adamah in Naphtali (Jos 19:36), a place.

senses.gloss: the ground that is tilled; soil
senses.definition: The soil that a man works and that gives plants, crops and food; cursed for the man’s sake, and blessed or withheld with the rain.

evidence.note: No plant of the field yet, for Yahweh God had not sent rain, “and there was no אָדָם to work הָאֲדָמָה”: man and ground made for each other.
“Out of הָאֲדָמָה Yahweh God made every tree to sprout.”
“Cursed is הָאֲדָמָה for your sake; in toil you shall eat of it all the days of your life.”
Cain “a worker of אֲדָמָה” brought “of the fruit of הָאֲדָמָה”.
“Buy us and our אֲדָמָה for bread … and give seed, that הָאֲדָמָה be not desolate”: farmland, bought and sown.
“The first of all the fruit of הָאֲדָמָה.”
“Rain for your seed with which you sow הָאֲדָמָה, and bread, the produce of הָאֲדָמָה.”
“He who works his אֲדָמָה shall be filled with bread.”
“The field is wasted, אֲדָמָה mourns, for the grain is wasted.”

senses.gloss: earth, as the stuff things are made of
senses.definition: Earth as a substance: what the man and the animals were formed from and go back to when they die, what an altar or a potter’s vessel is made of, and what is put on the head in mourning.

evidence.note: The man formed, “dust from הָאֲדָמָה”.
“Yahweh God formed out of הָאֲדָמָה every beast of the field and every bird of the heavens”: the animals of the same stuff.
“Until you return to הָאֲדָמָה, for out of it you were taken.”
“His breath goes out, he returns to his אֲדָמָה.”
“Many of those who sleep in אַדְמַת־עָפָר, ground of dust, shall awake”: where the dead lie, and from where they are raised.
“An altar of אֲדָמָה you shall make for me.”
Naaman asks for “two mules’ load of אֲדָמָה”.
“A potsherd among the potsherds of אֲדָמָה: shall the clay say to its former, What are you making?”
The bronze vessels cast “in the thick of הָאֲדָמָה”, in clay ground.
The runner from the battle, “his clothes torn and אֲדָמָה on his head”; so 2Sa 1:2; Neh 9:1.

senses.gloss: the ground underfoot; the face of the earth
senses.definition: The ground as a surface: what creatures creep on, what rain falls on and waters dry from, what opens and swallows; “the face of the ground” is the whole surface of the earth on which men and beasts live.

evidence.note: A mist “watered all the face of הָאֲדָמָה”.
“Every creeping thing of הָאֲדָמָה.”
The flood wiped out every living thing “that was on the face of הָאֲדָמָה”.
“Behold, the face of הָאֲדָמָה was dry.”
“The place on which you stand is אַדְמַת־קֹדֶשׁ, holy ground”; quoted Act 7:33.
“הָאֲדָמָה opens its mouth and swallows them … הָאֲדָמָה that was under them split.”
Moses, meek “above every אָדָם who was on the face of הָאֲדָמָה”.
“Until the day Yahweh gives rain on the face of הָאֲדָמָה.”
The unburied bones “shall be dung on the face of הָאֲדָמָה”.

senses.gloss: land: a people’s own soil, a country
senses.definition: The land a people lives on and lives from, their own soil: Egypt’s, and above all the land Yahweh swore to the fathers and gave to Israel, which they keep by obedience, are plucked from in exile, and are brought back to.

evidence.note: “That your days may be long on הָאֲדָמָה which Yahweh your God is giving you”; quoted Eph 6:2–3.
“To dwell on הָאֲדָמָה which Yahweh swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, to give them.”
To Jacob: “I will bring you back to this אֲדָמָה.”
“Joseph bought all the אֲדָמָה of Egypt for Pharaoh.”
“He will pluck Israel from this good אֲדָמָה which he gave to their fathers.”
“Your אֲדָמָה shall be divided by line, and you shall die on an unclean אֲדָמָה, and Israel shall surely go into exile from his אֲדָמָה.”
“I will plant them on their אֲדָמָה, and they shall no more be plucked up from their אֲדָמָה which I have given them.”
“I will open your graves and bring you up out of your graves, my people, and bring you to אַדְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל”: the phrase is Ezekiel’s own, about seventeen times.
“Your אֶרֶץ is desolate … your אֲדָמָה, strangers devour it before you.”
“How shall we sing Yahweh’s song on אַדְמַת נֵכָר, foreign ground?”
“He will make a covering for his אֲדָמָה, his people.”

senses.gloss: the earth, as where all peoples live
senses.definition: The whole inhabited ground: “the families of the ground”, “the peoples on the face of the ground”, are all mankind.

evidence.note: “In you all the families of הָאֲדָמָה shall be blessed”; so to Jacob, Gen 28:14; quoted Act 3:25.
“You only have I known of all the families of הָאֲדָמָה.”
“Out of all the peoples that are on the face of הָאֲדָמָה.”
Yahweh will visit “the kings of הָאֲדָמָה on הָאֲדָמָה”, set against the host of the height.

evidence.locator: Gen.2.7, הָאֲדָמָה → γῆς; Gen.12.3 and Gen.28.14 → γῆς; Exo.3.5 → γῆ; Exo.20.12 → γῆς; γῆ renders אֲדָמָה ×197

evidence.note: Gen 12:3; 28:14 quoted: “in your seed shall all the families of the γῆ be blessed”.
Exo 3:5 quoted: “the place where you stand is γῆ ἁγία”.
Exo 20:12 quoted: “that you may be long-lived on the γῆ”.
Gen 2:7 expounded: “the first man is ἐκ γῆς, of dust”.

parallels.note: Dust is what the ground is made of; the two stand together for what man is made of and returns to.

evidence.note: “Dust from the ground.”
“Return to the ground … to dust you shall return.”
“Trouble does not come out of dust, nor does toil sprout from אֲדָמָה.”

parallels.note: Earth or land beside ground, in parallel lines or in one sentence.

evidence.note: “To אַדְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל: an end! The end has come on the four corners of הָאָרֶץ.”
Wiped out “on the face of הָאֲדָמָה … wiped from הָאָרֶץ”.

parallels.note: Field and ground as the farmer’s land.

evidence.note: Each Egyptian sold “his field”, and Joseph bought “all the אֲדָמָה of Egypt”.

opposites.note: The height, the heavens, set against the ground.

evidence.note: “The host of the height in the height, and the kings of the ground on the ground.”

phrases.gloss: the face of the ground: the surface of the earth

evidence.note: “You send your breath, they are created, and you renew the face of אֲדָמָה.”

phrases.gloss: a worker of ground: one who tills the soil

evidence.note: “I am no prophet; a man working אֲדָמָה am I.”
Noah, אִישׁ הָאֲדָמָה, “man of the ground”, planted a vineyard.

phrases.gloss: the families of the ground: all the peoples of the earth
the ground of Israel: Israel’s own land (Ezekiel)

evidence.note: “I will gather you from the peoples … and give you אַדְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל.”
“Yahweh will inherit Judah as his portion on אַדְמַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ.”

phrases.gloss: the fruit of the ground: crops

words.summary: The colour of blood and of treading grapes; also of a cow, a horse, a stew of lentils and a healthy man’s skin, so a range from blood red to red-brown. In Gen 25:30 Esau calls the stew simply “the red, this red”, and the same tokens are filed a second time (a.bd.ae) as a noun for that dish. The key also counts the place Adummim (Jos 15:7; 18:17), “the red ones”.

senses.definition: Red: the colour scripture likens to blood and to garments stained in the winepress, and uses of a cow, horses and lentil stew.

evidence.note: Moab saw the water in the morning sun “אֲדֻמִּים like blood”, and said, “This is blood.”
“Why is your clothing אָדֹם, and your garments like his who treads in the winepress?”, answered in verse 3, “their juice spattered on my garments”; asked of the one coming “from Edom” (63:1).
“Let me gulp some of הָאָדֹם הָאָדֹם הַזֶּה, the red, this red … therefore his name was called Edom”; the dish was lentil stew (25:34).
“A cow, אֲדֻמָּה, whole, in which is no blemish”, burned for the water of impurity.
A man riding on a horse, אָדֹם, and behind him horses red, sorrel and white.
In the first chariot horses אֲדֻמִּים; taken up in Rev 6:4, ἵππος πυρρός.

senses.definition: Of a man in health: red-skinned, ruddy, said in praise beside “dazzling white”.

evidence.note: “My beloved is dazzling and אָדוֹם, marked out among ten thousand.”

evidence.locator: Zec.1.8, אָדֹם → πυρρόν, אֲדֻמִּים → πυρροί; Zec.6.2, אֲדֻמִּים → πυρροί; Gen.25.30 → πυρροῦ

evidence.note: “in LXX for אֱדֹם”; Rev 6:4; 12:3.
“Another horse went out, πυρρός, and to him who sat on it was given to take peace from the earth”: the red horse of Zec 1:8; 6:2, here the colour of bloodshed.
“A great dragon, πυρρός.”

words.summary: Ten uses in four stems; seven are the one participle מְאָדָּם, “reddened”, six of them the ram skins of the tabernacle’s covering.

senses.definition: Of the body in health: to be red, ruddier than coral, beside “purer than snow, whiter than milk”. One use.

evidence.note: “Her Nazirites were purer than snow, whiter than milk; they were אָדְמוּ in body more than corals.”

senses.definition: Made red: of ram skins prepared for the tabernacle’s covering, and of the shields of an army.

evidence.note: “Ram skins מְאָדָּמִים, reddened”, among the materials of the offering.
“A covering for the tent of ram skins reddened.”
“The shield of his mighty men is מְאָדָּם, the men of valour are in scarlet.”

senses.definition: To show red: of sins, red as crimson dye, set against the white of snow and wool. One use.

evidence.note: “Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be white as snow; though they יַאְדִּימוּ like crimson, they shall be as wool”; the hands of verse 15 are “full of blood”.

senses.definition: To show itself red: of wine in the cup. One use.

evidence.note: “Do not look on wine when it יִתְאַדָּם, when it gives its eye in the cup.”

words.summary: אָדֹם with its last two letters repeated, as יְרַקְרַק “greenish” (in the same verses) is made from יָרֹק. Six uses, all in the law of skin disease, and no cognate of the same form.

senses.definition: A weaker or mixed red: the colour of a diseased spot in skin, cloth, leather or a wall, named beside white and beside greenish.

evidence.note: “A bright spot, white, אֲדַמְדָּמֶת”: white tinged with red.
“If the mark is greenish (יְרַקְרַק) or אֲדַמְדָּם in the garment or in the skin.”
Hollows in the walls of a house, “greenish or reddish”.

words.summary: Three uses, of two people: Esau at birth and David as a youth.

senses.definition: Red in skin or hair: of Esau, who came out red and hairy, and of David, where it is joined to good looks.

evidence.note: “The first came out אַדְמוֹנִי, all of him like a cloak of hair, and they called his name Esau.”
David: “he was אַדְמוֹנִי, with beautiful eyes and good to look at.”
Goliath despised him, “for he was a youth, and אַדְמֹנִי, with a fair appearance”.

words.summary: Three uses, always first in a list of stones. The verses name the stone and do not describe it, so that it is red rests on the form of the word alone; which stone it is (carnelian, ruby) the text does not say.

senses.definition: The first stone of the first row of the breastplate of judgment, and the first of the stones that covered the king of Tyre in Eden.

evidence.note: “A row of אֹדֶם, פִּטְדָה and בָּרֶקֶת, the first row.”
“Every precious stone was your covering: אֹדֶם, פִּטְדָה …”

evidence.locator: Exo.28.17, אֹדֶם → σάρδιον; so Exo.39.10; Ezk.28.13

evidence.note: “in LXX for אֹדֶם, Ex 28:17, al.”; Rev 4:3; 21:20.
The sixth foundation of the city’s wall, in a list of twelve stones as on the breastplate.
He who sat on the throne was “in appearance like a jasper stone and a sardius”.

senses.definition: Doeg, a servant of Saul, is identified by the people he belongs to. Deuteronomy calls the Edomite Israel’s brother, and Genesis traces the Edomites to Esau.

cognates.note: The same collective as the Hebrew. In the Keret text El is ab adm, “father of adm”.

evidence.note: “adm ‘man(kind)’ (H. ʾādām)”.
tṣmt.adm.ṣat.špš, “she smites the men of sunrise (lit., of the going out of the sun)”.
The text has ab.adm twice, of El.
“man, individual; man, mankind, people”.

cognates.gloss: person, man; human being; commoner; (pl.) people
cognates.note: Phoenician and Punic. As in Hebrew it is “any person” in a prohibition (KAI 13.3–4, “whoever you are, any ʾdm”), and the commoner over against one of royal line (KAI 14.6–9), as “sons of אָדָם” stand against “sons of אִישׁ” (Psa 49:3). Unlike Hebrew it has a plural, ʾdmm.

evidence.note: “[Heb. ʾādām] n.m. 1. PERSON, MAN”, KAI 13.3/4; “2. HUMAN BEING”; “3. COMMONER (in contrast to mmlkt, person of royal lineage)”, KAI 14.6/9; “4. pl. PEOPLE”, KAI 14.6.

evidence.locator: SEM000968 ʾdm [man] N, PUN000032 ʾdm [person] N

evidence.note: “man; commoner; the first man”.

cognates.gloss: servants, serfs; clients, subject tribes; worshipers of a god
cognates.note: Sabaean, a collective noun like אָדָם, but of people in their dependence on a lord, king or god, not of mankind. Whether it is the same word narrowed, or another, is not settled, so it is recorded as possible only.

evidence.note: “n coll … (1) SERVANTS, SERFS of a landowner”, C609/2; “(2) CLIENTS, SUBJECT TRIBES of a king”, R4188/3; “(3) WORSHIPERS of a god”, J561b/6.

cognates.note: The name in Arabic is taken from the Hebrew, as the Arabic lexicographers themselves say; آدَمِيّ, “of Adam”, is their word for a human being. It is not independent evidence for the Hebrew noun.

evidence.note: “[Adam,] the father of mankind … there are various opinions respecting its derivation; but … the truth is that it is a foreign word, [i. e. Hebrew,] of the measure فَاعَلُ”.
“[Of, or relating to, Adam: and hence, human: and a human being:] a rel. n. from آدَمُ.”

cognates.note: Neo-Punic, once: the people “who dwell in the land”, as אֲדָמָה is a people’s land.

evidence.note: “[Heb. ʾădāmā] n.f. LAND”, KAI 145 I 3 (NPu) lʿm ʾyšb ʾdmt, “for the people who dwell in the land”.

evidence.locator: SEM000969 ʾdmt [ground] N, PUN000035 ʾdmt [land] N

cognates.note: The Targum’s word for אֲדָמָה in Gen 2:5. It may be the Hebrew word carried over by the translators and not a native Aramaic one; scripture’s own Aramaic uses אֲרַע.

evidence.note: “(= h. אֲדָמָה) earth. Targ. O. Gen. II, 5; a. fr.”
“earth, soil, dust”; “Compare Hebrew אֲדָמָה.”

cognates.note: Syriac, given as taken from the Hebrew. The Peshitta New Testament does not use it (SEDRA has no such lexeme); it writes ܐܪܥܐ, as in 1Co 15:47, “of dust, from the earth”.

evidence.note: “earth, soil, dust; ground, land; starch”; “From Hebrew אֲדָמָה (ʾăḏāmâ).”

cognates.gloss: dark red earth (used as a dye); dark blood
cognates.note: One Akkadian word names a dark red earth and dark blood: the ground and the colour together, and the colour as that of blood, as 2Ki 3:22 likens אָדֹם to blood. A plant of the same name is glossed “with red blossoms?”.

evidence.locator: armep x000083730, adamatu N, “(a dark red earth used as dye)”
cmawro x000000240, adamatu [(a plant)] N, senses “(a plant)”, “dark red earth”
armep x000083710, adamatu [(red blood)] N, senses “(a dark-coloured bodily discharge)”, “dark blood”

cognates.gloss: tanned or red hide, skin; the surface of the earth or ground
cognates.note: Arabic uses one word for a hide tanned red and, by a figure, for the surface of the ground, the earth’s “skin”; أَدَمَة is the inner skin and the interior or surface of the earth. It goes with אֲדָמָה as the face of the ground, and with the ram skins מְאָדָּמִים, “reddened”, of Exo 25:5.

evidence.note: “Tanned skin or hide; leather … or red skin or hide … when it is complete [in its tanning] and has become red”; “also signifies (tropical:) The surface of the earth or ground”.
“[The inner skin; the cutis, or derma;]”; “And (assumed tropical:) The interior of the earth or ground; the surface thereof being called its أَدِيم: or, as some say, its surface.”

cognates.gloss: a tawny or dark colour of skin (of people, camels, gazelles); tawny, dark-complexioned
cognates.note: A colour word of the same root, used of the skin of people and animals as אָדֹם and אַדְמוֹנִי are; the Arabic is brown or tawny where the Hebrew is red. The Arabic lexicographers derive it from “the colour of the earth”, the link between the colour and the ground that the Hebrew words suggest.

evidence.note: “in human beings, a tawny colour; or darkness of complexion … or intense سُمْرَة [or tawniness]; and it is said to be from أُدْمَةُ الأَرْضِ, meaning the colour of the earth”.
“Of the colour termed أُدْمَةٌ … applied to a human being, آدَمُ signifies tawny; or dark-complexioned”.

cognates.gloss: become red; redden oneself, put on red
cognates.note: The verb “be red” outside Hebrew, in the same language that has adm “mankind”: the two groups stand side by side in Ugaritic as in Hebrew.

evidence.note: “to become red, turn the colour red; to rouge oneself, to put on red make-up”.

evidence.locator: SEM000553 ʾdm [red] V, UGC000095 ʾdm V; HEB000115 ʾadam [red] V

cognates.gloss: be red (as listed); the adjective ʾädam is “delightful, pleasant, beautiful”
cognates.note: The root list gives a Geʿez verb ʾadama under “red”, but the Geʿez word found in a dictionary entry here means “pleasant, beautiful”, nearer to Arabic أَدَمَ “season, make agreeable” than to the colour. Possible only, until the verb is checked in Dillmann or Leslau.

evidence.locator: SEM000553 ʾdm [red] V, GEZ000092 ʾadama [red] V

evidence.note: “delightful, pleasant, sweet, beautiful; venerable, good”.

cognates.note: In the Targums and Talmud “blood” is written with a first א. It is the common word דְּמָא with a helping vowel before it, not a separate root, so it does not show that דָּם “blood” belongs to אדמ; but it shows how near the two sounded, as in Gen 9:6, דַּם הָאָדָם.

evidence.note: “(= דָּם, דְּמָא) blood. Targ. I Chron. XXII, 7; a. e. … Pl. אַדְמִין.”

doctrine.statement: “Yahweh God formed the man, dust from the ground (הָאָדָם עָפָר מִן־הָאֲדָמָה), and breathed into his nostrils breath of life, and the man became a living soul” (Gen 2:7). The beasts and birds were formed out of the same ground (Gen 2:19) and are called by the same words, living soul (Gen 1:24). The sentence on the man was to go back to it: “until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; for dust you are, and to dust you shall return” (Gen 3:19). The rest of scripture speaks the same way: “his breath goes out, he returns to his ground; in that day his thoughts perish” (Psa 146:4); “all flesh would expire together, and man return to dust” (Job 34:15); “as this one dies so that one dies, and one breath is for all, and man has no advantage over the beast … all are of the dust and all return to the dust” (Ecc 3:19–20); “you turn man back to dust, and say, Return, sons of man” (Psa 90:3). The hope held out is not that something of the man lives on, but that he will be woken: “many of those who sleep in ground of dust shall awake, some to life of the age” (Dan 12:2). Paul says the same of the first man, “out of earth, of dust”, and of all who bear his image (1Co 15:47–49). From the verses: man is made of the ground and is a living soul only while breath is in him; at death he returns to the ground and his thoughts perish; his hope is to be raised out of it.

Paul reads Gen 2:7 as the first half of a pair: “the first man Adam became a living soul; the last Adam a life-giving spirit … the first man is out of earth, of dust; the second man, the Lord out of heaven … and as we have borne the image of the one of dust, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly one” (1Co 15:45–49). He sets the two side by side as man and man: “since through a man came death, through a man also came resurrection of the dead; for as in Adam all die, so also in the Christ all shall be made alive” (1Co 15:21–22). In Romans the one man’s act is answered by the other’s: “through one man sin entered into the world, and death through sin, and so death passed to all men” (Rom 5:12); Adam “is a type of the one to come” (Rom 5:14); “as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one the many shall be made righteous” (Rom 5:19); the gift is “by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ” (Rom 5:15). From the verses: death came into the world by the sin of the first man and reaches all who are his; the one through whom life comes is likewise a man, called Adam and “the second man”, whose obedience undoes the first man’s disobedience; and those who now bear the image of the man of dust will bear his image when they are raised.

“God created the man in his image … male and female he created them” on the sixth day (Gen 1:27, 31), and “called their name Adam in the day they were created” (Gen 5:2). Moses dates history from that day: “ask now of the former days … from the day that God created man on the earth” (Deu 4:32), and the commandment rests on the week, “in six days Yahweh made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them” (Exo 20:11). Jesus cites the account as what happened: “from the beginning of the creation God made them male and female” (Mrk 10:6). The generations are then counted by years from Adam: he lived 130 years and begot Seth, and “all the days that Adam lived were 930 years, and he died” (Gen 5:3–5); the Chronicler begins his genealogy “Adam, Seth, Enosh” (1Ch 1:1), Luke ends his at “Adam, son of God” (Luk 3:38), and Jude counts Enoch “the seventh from Adam” (Jud 14). Paul tells the Athenians that God “made of one every nation of men to dwell on all the face of the earth” (Act 17:26). In the days of Noah “all flesh expired … and all mankind”, and only Noah and those with him in the ark were left (Gen 7:21–23). From the verses: mankind began with one man, made by God on the sixth day of the creation week and not descended from any earlier creature; all nations come from him; and the line from him to Christ is given as a counted line of fathers and sons.

“Let us make man in our image, according to our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the heavens and the cattle and all the earth” (Gen 1:26): the image is spoken in one breath with the rule. Adam in turn “begot in his likeness, according to his image” (Gen 5:3), and after the flood man is still said to be made in God’s image, which is why his blood may not be shed (Gen 9:6) nor he be cursed (Jas 3:9). Psalm 8 takes up Genesis 1: “what is man … you made him a little lower than the angels and crowned him with glory and honour; you made him rule over the works of your hands; you put all things under his feet” (Psa 8:5–7). “The heavens are Yahweh’s heavens, but the earth he has given to the sons of man” (Psa 115:16). Hebrews says of the psalm, “now we do not yet see all things subjected to him; but we see Jesus … crowned with glory and honour” (Heb 2:8–9), and Paul applies “he put all things under his feet” to Christ’s reign until death itself is destroyed (1Co 15:25–27). From the verses: man was made to bear God’s likeness and to rule the earth for him; that purpose stands, it has not yet been seen in mankind, and it is fulfilled in a man, Jesus, and on the earth that was given to the sons of man.

Scripture sets אָדָם against אֵל as it sets flesh against spirit: “Egypt is man and not God, and their horses flesh and not spirit” (Isa 31:3). To the ruler who said “I am a god” Yahweh answers, “you are man and not God”, and proves it by his death at the hand of those who pierce him (Ezk 28:2, 9). “God is not a man that he should lie, nor a son of man that he should change his mind” (Num 23:19; so 1Sa 15:29). No man can see him and live (Exo 33:20). From the verses: to be אָדָם is to be what God is not, a creature of flesh who can die. The one mediator “of God and of men” is named on the side of men: “a man (ἄνθρωπος), Christ Jesus” (1Ti 2:5).

The ground was cursed for the man’s sake (Gen 3:17), and Lamech named Noah in hope of comfort “from the ground which Yahweh has cursed” (Gen 5:29). The promise to Abraham and to Jacob answers the curse with blessing in the same word: “in you all the families of the ground shall be blessed” (Gen 12:3; 28:14), which Peter preaches as the covenant now being fulfilled through God’s servant Jesus (Act 3:25–26). The land sworn to the fathers is called their ground (Deu 30:20), and the prophets promise a return to it that will not be undone: “I will plant them on their ground, and they shall no more be plucked up” (Amo 9:15). Ezekiel joins that return to resurrection: “I will open your graves and bring you up out of your graves, my people, and bring you to the ground of Israel … and I will put my spirit in you and you shall live, and I will set you on your own ground” (Ezk 37:12–14). Paul says the creation itself, subjected to futility, “shall be set free from the bondage of corruption into the freedom of the glory of the children of God” (Rom 8:20–21). From the verses: the blessing God has promised is for the families of the ground, on the ground; Israel’s hope is its own soil, reached through the opening of graves; and the curse laid on the ground for Adam’s sake is to be lifted from it.

note: Drafted 2026-11-15. Root key אדמ, as the brief and the database key it; no other entry has it. One spelling, three groups (man, ground, red), kept together: scripture joins אָדָם and אֲדָמָה in Gen 2:7; 3:19, 23, and the cognates join ground and colour (Akkadian adamatu “dark red earth”, Arabic أُدْمَة “the colour of the earth”, أَدِيم “red hide; surface of the ground”). Scripture does not itself say that the man or the ground is named from the colour, and the summary says so; the reviewer should check that wording. There is no merged letter in the root, so no `sounds`. דָּם “blood” is NOT taken into this entry: it is filed under its own key, every language has it without the א (Akkadian dāmu, Phoenician dm, Krahmalkov p. 149), and the Aramaic אֲדָם / אַדְמָא “blood” is דְּמָא with a helping vowel (recorded as cognate arc-adma, possible). What ties blood to this root is only the likeness of 2Ki 3:22 and the sound play of Gen 9:6, and Akkadian adamatu “dark blood”. Names and places left to name entries or left out: אֱדוֹם (a.bd.af) is in names/edom.json. Its gentilic אֲדֹמִי (a.bd.ag) is a word here; Adam the man has names/adam.json, with no bdb key of its own because a.bc.ab is the noun’s (the name’s tokens, Gen 4:25; 5:1–5; 1Ch 1:1 and the unpointed-article forms לְאָדָם in Gen 2:20; 3:17, 21, are counted here). Places, not drafted: אַדְמָה Admah (a.bc.ad), אֲדָמִי הַנֶּקֶב (a.bc.ae), the town אָדָם (Jos 3:16, inside a.bc.ab), אֲדָמָה in Naphtali (Jos 19:36, inside a.bc.ac), Adummim (Jos 15:7; 18:17, inside a.bd.ac). אַדְמָתָא (a.bd.ak, Est 1:14) is a Persian prince’s name with nothing in scripture tying it to this root; not drafted. עֹבֵד אֱדוֹם is a person’s name (Obed-edom@2Sa.6.10) made of עבד and Edom, filed under עבד (p.ac.af); not drafted here. a.bd.ae (אֱדֹם, 11 tokens) is the same tokens as a.bd.ac filed a second time as a noun for the red stew of Gen 25:30; only a.bd.ac is named, as the README directs. Hos 6:7 (כְּאָדָם “like Adam” or “like men”) and Job 31:33 are not cited for a sense because either reading fits. The son-of-man doctrine is already in ben.json and enosh.json and is not repeated; בֶּן־אָדָם is given here as a phrase. No Aramaic word: Daniel and Ezra use אֱנָשׁ, and the Peshitta New Testament has from this root only the names ܐܕܡ (SEDRA lexeme 32) and ܐܕܘܡ Idumaea (lexeme 30, Mrk 3:8), which are in the name entries. Greek: Ἀδάμ is a loan (Abbott-Smith); σάρδιον is cited from the Septuagint’s rendering, though the TR at Rev 21:20 reads σάρδιος and at Rev 4:3 σάρδινος. Act 15:17 (Amo 9:12, Edom read as “men”) is recorded under ἄνθρωπος as scripture’s own reading of the consonants. Page checks: Krahmalkov pp. 32–34 and Biella p. 5 from the scans’ text and running heads; Segert pp. 93, 166, 178 from the scan’s text (the section number of the Keret extract was not legible, so only the page and KTU reference are given, and “El” as the bearer of ab adm is from the Keret text itself, not from a gloss of Segert’s). Leads not followed: DULAT for Ugaritic adm (noun and verb) and its ab adm; Akkadian adamu / adammu “blood; red garment; important person” (Wiktionary’s list; CAD A/1 not checked; Oracc has only a Sumerian-glossary adamum “a red garment”, Ur III); Akkadian Udumu and Egyptian jdwmꜥ for Edom (TLA lemma not found); Geʿez ʾadama in Dillmann or Leslau (recorded as possible from the root list only); Syriac ܐܕܡܬܐ in Payne Smith (cited from Wiktionary only); Edomite and Moabite ʾdm “man” (Wiktionary only); the proposed link of Arabic أَنَام “creatures” with אָדָם; Akkadian adnātu “world, people”. Open questions for review: (1) whether the red words’ cognates are rightly named on אֲדַמְדָּם, אַדְמוֹנִי and אֹדֶם, which have no cognate of their own form; (2) the kin link between “the man” and “earth as stuff”, which rests on Gen 2:7 alone; (3) the Sabaean ʾdm “servants” as possible; (4) the wording of the doctrine statements, especially image-of-god and kingdom-of-god.
